claims: John F. Kennedy Jr. was cremated.
John F. Kennedy Jr.'s ashes were scattered at sea on July 22, 1999.
The ceremony scattering John F. Kennedy Jr.'s ashes was aboard the USS Briscoe.
John F. Kennedy Jr.'s ashes were scattered in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts.
The burial of John F. Kennedy Jr. took place near the site of the plane crash that killed John F. Kennedy Jr., Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, and Lauren Bessette.
Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy was John F. Kennedy Jr.'s wife.
Lauren Bessette was Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy's sister.
John F. Kennedy Jr.'s ashes were scattered in the Atlantic Ocean approximately 7–8 miles off the coast of Martha's Vineyard.
17 family members from the Kennedy and Bessette families attended the private ceremony.
John F. Kennedy Jr. piloted the plane.
The plane plunged into the ocean on July 16, 1999.
The plane plunge resulted in the instant death of all three passengers.
The instant death of all three passengers was due to multiple traumatic injuries.
The burial at sea was chosen to honor John F. Kennedy Jr.'s wish to be cremated.
The burial at sea was chosen to avoid a media circus
